That PTC thermistor isn't in the circuit for temperature control. It is in there for inrush current limiting. If it blew the PTC, then your compressor is drawing a lot of current on startup. You may have a bad motor start/run capacitor that is making the current spike when the compressor switches on. Your new PTC could blow too if the fault is in the capacitor or the motor. Do you have a Kill-O-Watt meter or a clamp ammeter to measure the current draw when the compressor starts and runs? It might be difficult to capture the start current with either device, but if the run current exceeds the rated operation current on the label then you have another problem besides the blown PTC.
